subject: Discovery: HealthSync LLM API portability & compatibility checklist
content:
Message 1
-----Original Message-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: HealthSync LLM API portability & compatibility checklist

Hi Samira —

Great to meet you earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps. I kept this to the essentials so we can pick the right technical/contract path quickly.

Pain points you shared:
- Vendor lock on proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic) causing cost unpredictability and export challenges for on-prem work.
- Need deterministic latency for user-facing clinical triage use cases (95th pct target < 250ms for short prompts).
- Audit/compliance: requirement to retain audit logs and control model weights for regulated customers.

Current stack & usage (your estimates):
- OpenAI: embeddings + completion-heavy workflows (~1.2M tokens/month).
- Anthropic: chat for conversational triage (approx 150k turns/month).
- Fronting layer: custom router that decorates prompts and enforces rate limits; currently tightly coupled to provider SDKs.

Success criteria for a migration:
1) API compatibility with minimal code changes (prefer SDK/adapter layer approach).
2) Output parity within acceptable delta for our clinical templates (we discussed using 20 sample prompts as an eval set).
3) Predictable unit economics (targeting <= 40% cost reduction at parity latency).
4) Ops controls: key management, VPC deployment option, and SLA for dedicated capacity.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial):
- Llama-3-13B (quantized variant) — candidate for cost-sensitive embeddings/completions
- Mistral Mix/ChaCha family (if abstraction supports chat context management)
- Anthropic-compatible chat shim variants (to preserve system/prompt semantics)

Attachments I’m sharing: healthsync-current-stack.xlsx (high-level inventory you started), and a first-pass Redwood compatibility matrix (redwood-compatibility-matrix.pdf) that maps common SDK calls to our adapter suggestions.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Diego to review HealthSync stack and confirm adapter surface area (target: tech deep dive next week).
2) HealthSync to send 20 canonical prompts + 3 example convo flows for parity evals.
3) I’ll put together a scoped proposal (SE + runtime sizing + cost estimate) and a draft mutual action plan by EOW.

If I missed anything from our call, flag it back and I’ll update.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Message 2
From: Samira Patel <samira@healthsync.ai>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: HealthSync LLM API portability & compatibility checklist

Thanks Neha — this is a clean summary and matches our notes. A few clarifications so Diego has context before the deep dive: 

1) Volume nuance: the 1.2M tokens is peak-month; our current steady-state is closer to ~650k. Embeddings calls are bursty (nightly batch jobs + realtime small-batch inference).
2) Prompts: we’ll share 20 canonical prompts by Monday. Several are templated with PHI redaction steps — we redacted locally before sending.
3) Latency SLA: 95th pct < 250ms applies to our shortest prompts (<= 128 tokens). For longer generation paths we tolerate higher latency.

We tried an internal pilot with an LLM-hosted self-managed option last quarter but ran into memory/kv-cache scaling issues under concurrent load (130+ concurrent users). That’s why we care about Redwood’s autoscaling/burst behavior for Dedicated.

I’ve attached an export with API call examples and a small sample of the message templates for parity testing.

Samira
Head of Product, HealthSync Solutions
samira@healthsync.ai | +1 (650) 555-4444
